title: How long is the day at each place?
description: Graphs of sunrise and sunset times across the year at four places in India are read. The video tells the sunrise line from the sunset line, finds the earliest sunrise in January, and finds the day length as the gap between the two lines.
teaching_notes: One idea: the lower line is sunrise and the upper line is sunset, and the gap between them is the length of the day. Watch for students who read one line only.

source: Figure it Out (more on mean and median, question 14)
video_script.why: The child can read a peak from a line and now reads two lines together, and takes the gap between them.
video_script.substitution: Tell the two lines apart by the time of day, read one value in a month, and take the gap between the lines for the day length.
video_script.anchor: the book's graphs of sunrise and sunset times across the year at four locations in India
video_script.payoff_line: read the values from the graph and give them as approximate

final_answer.value: Read the values from the graph and give them as approximate
final_answer.spoken: read the values from the graph and give them as approximate

never_show: the sunset line is the lower line
maths_rules: sunrise is the earlier time of the day, so its line is the lower line; sunset is the upper line
(i) find the lowest sunrise value in January across the four places
day length = sunset time - sunrise time
(ii) the longest day over the year is where the gap between the sunset line and the sunrise line is widest
(iii) open: share what the lines show, for example a smooth up and down pattern that repeats each year
slip: day length is the gap between the two lines, not the height of one line
video_script.design: One idea: tell the lines apart, read one place in one month, and take the gap between the two lines. The graphs stay on screen all video; no values are invented.
open_questions: The graph values are not in the extracted book text, so the place with the earliest sunrise and the day lengths cannot be checked; the video gives the method, and the readings are left to the figure.
